identity.title: A "knob-in-hole" gate in the antibody C(H)1 domain underlies subclass-independent IgA hinge cleavage by the commensal metallopeptidase IgAse.

content.abstract: Human immunoglobulin (Ig) A (IgA) protects  approximately 400 m(2) of mucosae from microbes. Bacterial IgA-peptidases subvert this defense by cleaving the F(ab)-F(c) hinge of subclass IgA1 while sparing the hinge-divergent, colon-dominant IgA2 subclass. The exception is IgAse, a  approximately 140-kDa, seven-domain, membrane-bound metallopeptidase from the colonic commensal Thomasclavelia ramosa that targets both subclasses but no other protein. We previously narrowed the minimal functional assembly down to the IgAse catalytic and wrapping domains (CD and WD) plus the IgA1/2 F(ab)', i.e., the hinge and a F(ab) of light and heavy chains (LC, HC), each with a variable and a constant Ig domain (V(L) + C(L), V(H) + C(H)1). The transient interaction culminates in cleavage of a proline-valine bond within the first two hinge residues, downstream of a conserved C-terminal C(H)1 disulfide (SS2). Here, single-particle cryoelectron microscopy of a disulfide-stabilized minimal IgAse:IgA2 F(ab)' complex yielded high-quality density strongly supporting two states along the cleavage reaction coordinate, a "recognition complex" and a subsequent "precatalytic complex," in which F(ab)' binds frontally to the IgAse CD via a C(H)1 beta-sheet and overhang loop LbetaEbetaF. This loop binds like a knob to a preformed hole in the active-site cleft. Binding rearranges the knob and rotates SS2  approximately  180 degrees , enabling access of the hinge into the cleft of the otherwise unaffected precatalytic complex. Together, this work defines a unique, C(H)1-mediated hinge-delivering "gate" mechanism, validated by a crystal structure of unbound IgA2 F(ab), point mutations disrupting the C(H)1:CD interface, and molecular dynamics calculations, which provide the structural framework for subclass-independent IgA cleavage.
